Career Pathway
Business Intelligence & Analytics


NAICS Code
NAICS: 541512


Industry Label
54 (Sector): Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services  — 5415 (Industry Group): Computer Systems Design and Related Services  — — 541512 (National Industry): Computer Systems Design Services


Relevancy
NAICS code 541512 covers firms that implement technology systems. This is a broad categorization but can cover areas such as developing custom data pipelines, BI tools, and machine learning solutions (listed as Information management computer systems integration design services under the NAICS index [1]).  This NAICS category is thus the most relevant for students targeting roles in analytics, data science, machine learning, business intelligence, analytics or data engineering, or closely related data careers.



[1]: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) U.S. Census Bureau. (n.d.). https://www.census.gov/naics/?input=5415&year=2022&details=541512

title: Introduction
text:
Business intelligence (BI) and analytics professionals occupy a distinct and growing segment of the technology labor market. These professionals sit at the intersection of technical data skills and business stakeholder communication. Unlike data scientists who build predictive models or machine learning engineers who deploy algorithms, BI analysts are responsible for translating operational data into dashboards, KPIs, and reports that drive decision quality and impact commercial outcomes for businesses. This role type is in high demand, highly varied across industries, and poorly served by existing career guidance tools.
Students and early-career professionals targeting BI and analytics roles face ambiguity of hiring expectations when it comes to which combination of tools, domain fluency, and communication skills will make them competitive. For example, someone fluent in SQL and Tableau competes for jobs that are different from someone else who is fluent in Power BI and DAX, but both would be hired as a “BI analyst”.
Current career advising tools do not always resolve this distinction. Furthermore, a key requirement of success in this career is strong stakeholder management skills, which evolve based on long-term career pathways. For example, a mid-career BI analyst growing into a senior technical IC will need command of a different set of skills as one growing into a more business-oriented manager.
This project addresses these gaps by building a data-driven career evaluation prototype scoped to NAICS 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services), a sector where BI and analytics roles are concentrated and quickly evolving, especially in the face of AI. The product is designed to help a BI-focused job seeker better understand their strengths and opportunities for upskilling.

title: Introduction
text:
2 Research and Product Rationale
The case for building this tool is anchored in three ideas:

Documented strong labor market growth in BI-specific occupations.
Documented transition in the BI tool landscape that has created new skill requirements, especially as AI handles more of the technical aspects of these roles, emphasizing skills that AI can’t (currently) tackle, such as framing business problems, bringing a deep understanding of a firm’s business model to BI solutioning, or Stakeholder management and accountability.
Connecting the gap between how students and professionals self-assess their BI readiness, versus what skills employers are actually looking for.

title: Introduction
text:
3 Literature Review
The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects 35 percent employment growth for data scientists, which is the broader occupational category that encompasses Business Intelligence Analysts (SOC 15-2051), from 2025 to 2035, with a median annual wage of $120,230, making it one of the fastest-growing and highest-compensating occupational groups in the U.S. economy U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (2024). This growth is driven by rising enterprise demand for real-time reporting, self-service analytics platforms, and KPI governance frameworks that require dedicated BI practitioners, not just ad-hoc report builders.
The World Economic Forum paces Business Intelligence Analysts third on its list of fastest-growing roles globally through 2027, behind only AI/ML Specialists and Sustainability Specialists, with Data Analysts and Scientists projected to add 1.4 million jobs, which a 30–35 percent increase World Economic Forum (2023).
Additionally, the BI tooling landscape has undergone a significant shift. The migration from on-premise reporting tools (Crystal Reports, SSRS) to cloud-native platforms (Tableau Cloud, Microsoft Power BI, Looker, Sigma) has redefined the core skill profile employers expect. Forrester Research notes that “BI technology has become largely commoditized,” with enterprises now prioritizing platforms native to cloud hyperscalers over legacy on-premise deployments Forrester Research (2023).

title: Introduction
section: 4 What we expect to explore and discover
text:
4 What we expect to explore and discover
We expect this project to surface three primary findings specific to the BI and analytics career pathway within NAICS 541512.
First, BI “Analyst” demand is concentrated around three roles, each with a fairly distinct skill set and salary range:

BI developer (tool-focused, platform implementation)
Analytics engineer (data modeling, dbt, Snowflake, visualization)
Analytics communicator (stakeholder-facing partnerships, KPI strategy, reporting governance)

A student who can identify which archetype matches their strengths will compete in a smaller, better-defined market than one who applies generically to all “BI analyst” roles.
Second, the broad tooling split between Power BI and Tableau represents a meaningful career specialization branch: employers who use one rarely use both, and compensation and industry concentration differ between firms employing either one. Power BI fluency tends to correlate with stronger demand in financial services and healthcare, while Tableau demand remains stronger in technology firms, but newer start ups tend to use more lightweight tools such as Basedash. Other tools may be required by firms in other industries. This has direct implications for how students should prioritize tool investment and learning.
Third, SQL proficiency is still key. SQL combined with at least one cloud data platform (Snowflake or BigQuery) and one BI visualization tool constitutes the minimum viable skill set for entry-level BI roles in NAICS 541512. From these foundational skill sets, a typical student should focus on upskilling based on target roles (e.g., communications, product analytics etc.). We would want to explore the top, varied combinations of SQL + Cloud Platform + BI tool + Role-specific needs that would make students competitive in the BI job market.

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("AD688_JobFacts") \
    .config("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "UTC") \
    .getOrCreate()
spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")

# Load from raw API CSV 
jobs_raw_spark = spark.read.csv(
    "./outputs/api_job_facts.csv",
    header=True,
    inferSchema=True,
    multiLine=True,
    escape='"'
)

FIELD_MAP = {
    "job_id":                                        "job_id",
    "posted_at":                                     "posted_at",
    "title":                                         "title",
    "normalized_title":                              "normalized_title",
    "company_name":                                  "company_name",
    "location_text":                                 "location_text",
    "city":                                          "city",
    "city_code":                                     "city_code",
    "state":                                         "state",
    "state_code":                                    "state_code",
    "remote_status":                                 "remote_status",
    "employment_type":                               "employment_type",
    "salary_text":                                   "salary_text",
    "annual_salary_min":                             "annual_salary_min",
    "annual_salary_max":                             "annual_salary_max",
    "hourly_salary_min":                             "hourly_salary_min",
    "hourly_salary_max":                             "hourly_salary_max",
    "soc_code":                                      "soc_code",
    "soc_name":                                      "soc_name",
    "occupation_family":                             "occupation_family",
    "naics_code":                                    "naics_code",
    "naics_name":                                    "naics_name",
    "onet_code":                                     "onet_code",
    "onet_name":                                     "onet_name",
    "cip_code":                                      "cip_code",
    "cip_name":                                      "cip_name",
    "skills":                                        "skills",
    "program_matches":                               "program_matches",
    "description":                                   "description",
    "bls.employment":                                "bls_employment",
    "bls.annual_mean_wage":                          "bls_annual_mean_wage",
    "bls.annual_median_wage":                        "bls_annual_median_wage",
    "bls.source_year":                               "bls_source_year",
    "student_signals.work_type":                     "student_signals_work_type",
    "student_signals.requirements_summary":          "student_signals_requirements_summary",
    "student_signals.responsibilities_summary":      "student_signals_responsibilities_summary",
    "student_signals.technical_tools_summary":       "student_signals_technical_tools_summary",
}

select_exprs = []
skipped = []
for src, alias in FIELD_MAP.items():
    if src in jobs_raw_spark.columns:
        # Backtick-quote any column name containing a dot (flat CSV column, not a struct)
        col_ref = F.col(f"`{src}`") if "." in src else F.col(src)
        select_exprs.append(col_ref.alias(alias))
    else:
        skipped.append(src)

if skipped:
    print(f"Columns not found (skipped): {skipped}")

jobs_selected = jobs_raw_spark.select(select_exprs)
jobs_selected.createOrReplaceTempView("job_facts_raw")
print(f"Selected {len(select_exprs)} columns — raw view registered as: job_facts_raw")
jobs_selected.printSchema()

jobs_clean = spark.sql("""

    WITH

    -- ── STEP 1: Remove noisy data ──────────────────────────────────────────
    -- Rows with null job_id are dropped; they cannot be keyed or joined.
    -- Rows with null title are dropped; they are unusable for downstream analysis.
    
    base AS (
        SELECT *
        FROM job_facts_raw
        WHERE job_id IS NOT NULL
          AND title IS NOT NULL
    ),

    -- ── STEP 2: Normalize categorical labels ─────────────────────────
    -- remote_status and employment_type arrive with inconsistent casing
    -- and freeform strings (e.g. "REMOTE", "Remote Work", "wfh").
    -- Map to four canonical values. 
    -- Any unrecognized value defaults to 'Unknown' rather than NULL so aggregations are more meaningful.
    labeled AS (
        SELECT *,

        CASE
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) IN ('remote', 'fully remote', 'work from home', 'wfh', 'remote work')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%remote%' AND LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) NOT LIKE '%partial%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%wfh%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%home%'
                THEN 'Remote'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) IN ('hybrid', 'hybrid remote', 'partial remote', 'hybrid/remote')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%hybrid%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%partial%'
                THEN 'Hybrid'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) IN ('on-site', 'onsite', 'in-office', 'in office', 'on site', 'office')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%office%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%site%'
                THEN 'On-site'
            ELSE 'Unknown'
        END AS remote_status_clean,

        CASE
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) IN ('full-time', 'full time', 'fulltime', 'ft', 'permanent')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%permanent%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%full%'
                THEN 'Full-time'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) IN ('part-time', 'part time', 'parttime', 'pt')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%part%'
                THEN 'Part-time'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) IN ('contract', 'contractor', 'temp', 'temporary', 'freelance', 'c2c')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%contract%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%temp%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%freelance%'
                THEN 'Contract'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) IN ('internship', 'intern', 'co-op', 'coop')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%intern%'
                THEN 'Internship'
            ELSE 'Unknown'
        END AS employment_type_clean


        FROM base
    ),

    -- ── STEP 3: Salary outlier handling ─────────────────────────────
    -- Salary fields contain a few data errors: $0, $1, implausibly high values from mis-parsed hourly-to-annual conversions, or potentially test records. 
    -- Values outside plausible BI/analytics bands are set to NULL (even without salary data, the post itself e.g. skills are useful)
    -- WHERE Annual band:  $20,000 – $500,000
    -- WHERE Hourly band:  $10  – $250
    -- WHERE NOT min > max (data entry error)
    -- WHERE NOT both are set to NULL.
    salaries AS (
        SELECT *,

            CASE
                WHEN CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 20000 AND 500000
                 AND CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 20000 AND 500000
                 AND CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE) <= CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                    THEN CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS annual_salary_min_clean,

            CASE
                WHEN CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 20000 AND 500000
                 AND CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 20000 AND 500000
                 AND CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE) <= CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                    THEN CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS annual_salary_max_clean,

            CASE
                WHEN CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 10 AND 250
                 AND CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 10 AND 250
                 AND CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE) <= CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                    THEN CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS hourly_salary_min_clean,

            CASE
                WHEN CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 10 AND 250
                 AND CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 10 AND 250
                 AND CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE) <= CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                    THEN CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS hourly_salary_max_clean

        FROM labeled
    )

    -- ── FINAL SELECT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    -- Replace raw categorical and salary columns with cleaned versions.
    -- All other optional fields (city, soc_code, bls_*, skills, etc.)
    SELECT
        job_id,
        posted_at,
        title,
        normalized_title,
        company_name,
        location_text,
        city,
        city_code,
        state,
        state_code,
        remote_status_clean                          AS remote_status,
        employment_type_clean                        AS employment_type,
        salary_text,
        annual_salary_min_clean                      AS annual_salary_min,
        annual_salary_max_clean                      AS annual_salary_max,
        hourly_salary_min_clean                      AS hourly_salary_min,
        hourly_salary_max_clean                      AS hourly_salary_max,
        soc_code,
        soc_name,
        occupation_family,
        naics_code,
        naics_name,
        onet_code,
        onet_name,
        cip_code,
        cip_name,
        skills,
        program_matches,
        description,
        bls_employment,
        bls_annual_mean_wage,
        bls_annual_median_wage,
        bls_source_year,
        student_signals_work_type,
        student_signals_requirements_summary,
        student_signals_responsibilities_summary,
        student_signals_technical_tools_summary

    FROM salaries

""")

# Register as the canonical SQL view for all downstream analysis
jobs_clean.createOrReplaceTempView("job_facts")
print(f"Clean rows: {jobs_clean.count()}")
jobs_clean.show(5, truncate=60)

jobs_clean.toPandas().to_csv("./outputs/api_job_facts_cleaned.csv", index=False)
print("Saved ./outputs/api_job_facts_cleaned.csv")

import os
import requests
import pandas as pd
from dotenv import load_dotenv, find_dotenv

import sys

#load_dotenv("M01_A/m01_data/.env")
#load_dotenv()

print(f"Working directory: {os.getcwd()}")

_env_candidates = [
    "M01_A/m01_data/.env",   # original relative path
    ".env",                   # project root
    "../.env",                # one level up
    find_dotenv(usecwd=True), # dotenv's own upward search
]

_loaded = False
for _p in _env_candidates:
    if _p and Path(_p).exists():
        load_dotenv(_p, override=True)
        print(f".env loaded from: {Path(_p).resolve()}")
        _loaded = True
        break

if not _loaded:
    print("No .env file found — relying on shell environment variables.")

API_KEY = os.getenv("EMPLOYABILITY_API_KEY", "").strip()
BASE_URL = os.getenv("EMPLOYABILITY_API_BASE_URL", "https://met-employability-services.azurewebsites.net").strip().rstrip("/")
STUDENT_API_BASE_URL = os.getenv("STUDENT_API_BASE_URL", "").strip().rstrip("/")

if not API_KEY:
    raise RuntimeError("EMPLOYABILITY_API_KEY is missing. Add it to .env before rendering this assignment.")
if not BASE_URL:
    raise RuntimeError("EMPLOYABILITY_API_BASE_URL is missing. Add it to .env before rendering this assignment.")
if not STUDENT_API_BASE_URL:
    if BASE_URL.endswith("/api/v1/student"):
        STUDENT_API_BASE_URL = BASE_URL
    elif BASE_URL.endswith("/met-career-match"):
        STUDENT_API_BASE_URL = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1"
    else:
        STUDENT_API_BASE_URL = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/student"

def api_url(path):
    return f"{STUDENT_API_BASE_URL}/{path.strip('/')}/"

headers = {"X-API-Key": API_KEY, "Accept": "application/json"}

schema_response = requests.get(api_url("schema"), timeout=30)
schema_response.raise_for_status()
print("Schema keys:", list(schema_response.json().keys())[:10])

#comment out to include all data
MAX_RECORDS = 1_000

all_rows = []
pull_log = []
params = {"naics": "5415", "limit": 200, "offset": 0}

while True:
    response = requests.get(api_url("jobs"), headers=headers, params=params, timeout=60)
    if response.status_code == 429:
        raise RuntimeError("Rate limited. Rerun later.")
    response.raise_for_status()
    payload = response.json()
    page = payload["results"]
    if not page:
        break
    all_rows.extend(page)
    pull_log.append({
        "offset": params["offset"],
        "limit": params["limit"],
        "status_code": response.status_code,
        "rows_returned": len(page),
    })
    print(f"offset={params['offset']} | page={len(page)} | total={len(all_rows)}")

    #comment out to include all data
    if len(all_rows) >= MAX_RECORDS:
        break

    params["offset"] += params["limit"]

jobs_raw = pd.json_normalize(all_rows)
jobs_raw["posted_at"] = pd.to_datetime(jobs_raw["posted_at"], errors="coerce", utc=True)
jobs_raw = jobs_raw[jobs_raw["posted_at"] >= pd.Timestamp("2026-01-01", tz="UTC")].copy()
print(f"Raw pull (after date filter): {jobs_raw.shape}")
print(jobs_raw.columns.tolist())

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("AD688_JobFacts") \
    .config("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "UTC") \
    .getOrCreate()
spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")

# Load from raw API CSV 
jobs_raw_spark = spark.read.csv(
    "./outputs/api_job_facts.csv",
    header=True,
    inferSchema=True,
    multiLine=True,
    escape='"'
)

FIELD_MAP = {
    "job_id":                                        "job_id",
    "posted_at":                                     "posted_at",
    "title":                                         "title",
    "normalized_title":                              "normalized_title",
    "company_name":                                  "company_name",
    "location_text":                                 "location_text",
    "city":                                          "city",
    "city_code":                                     "city_code",
    "state":                                         "state",
    "state_code":                                    "state_code",
    "remote_status":                                 "remote_status",
    "employment_type":                               "employment_type",
    "salary_text":                                   "salary_text",
    "annual_salary_min":                             "annual_salary_min",
    "annual_salary_max":                             "annual_salary_max",
    "hourly_salary_min":                             "hourly_salary_min",
    "hourly_salary_max":                             "hourly_salary_max",
    "soc_code":                                      "soc_code",
    "soc_name":                                      "soc_name",
    "occupation_family":                             "occupation_family",
    "naics_code":                                    "naics_code",
    "naics_name":                                    "naics_name",
    "onet_code":                                     "onet_code",
    "onet_name":                                     "onet_name",
    "cip_code":                                      "cip_code",
    "cip_name":                                      "cip_name",
    "skills":                                        "skills",
    "program_matches":                               "program_matches",
    "description":                                   "description",
    "bls.employment":                                "bls_employment",
    "bls.annual_mean_wage":                          "bls_annual_mean_wage",
    "bls.annual_median_wage":                        "bls_annual_median_wage",
    "bls.source_year":                               "bls_source_year",
    "student_signals.work_type":                     "student_signals_work_type",
    "student_signals.requirements_summary":          "student_signals_requirements_summary",
    "student_signals.responsibilities_summary":      "student_signals_responsibilities_summary",
    "student_signals.technical_tools_summary":       "student_signals_technical_tools_summary",
}

select_exprs = []
skipped = []
for src, alias in FIELD_MAP.items():
    if src in jobs_raw_spark.columns:
        # Backtick-quote any column name containing a dot (flat CSV column, not a struct)
        col_ref = F.col(f"`{src}`") if "." in src else F.col(src)
        select_exprs.append(col_ref.alias(alias))
    else:
        skipped.append(src)

if skipped:
    print(f"Columns not found (skipped): {skipped}")

jobs_selected = jobs_raw_spark.select(select_exprs)
jobs_selected.createOrReplaceTempView("job_facts_raw")
print(f"Selected {len(select_exprs)} columns — raw view registered as: job_facts_raw")
jobs_selected.printSchema()

jobs_clean = spark.sql("""

    WITH

    -- ── STEP 1: Remove noisy data ──────────────────────────────────────────
    -- Rows with null job_id are dropped; they cannot be keyed or joined.
    -- Rows with null title are dropped; they are unusable for downstream analysis.
    
    base AS (
        SELECT *
        FROM job_facts_raw
        WHERE job_id IS NOT NULL
          AND title IS NOT NULL
    ),

    -- ── STEP 2: Normalize categorical labels ─────────────────────────
    -- remote_status and employment_type arrive with inconsistent casing
    -- and freeform strings (e.g. "REMOTE", "Remote Work", "wfh").
    -- Map to four canonical values. 
    -- Any unrecognized value defaults to 'Unknown' rather than NULL so aggregations are more meaningful.
    labeled AS (
        SELECT *,

        CASE
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) IN ('remote', 'fully remote', 'work from home', 'wfh', 'remote work')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%remote%' AND LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) NOT LIKE '%partial%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%wfh%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%home%'
                THEN 'Remote'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) IN ('hybrid', 'hybrid remote', 'partial remote', 'hybrid/remote')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%hybrid%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%partial%'
                THEN 'Hybrid'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) IN ('on-site', 'onsite', 'in-office', 'in office', 'on site', 'office')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%office%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(remote_status)) LIKE '%site%'
                THEN 'On-site'
            ELSE 'Unknown'
        END AS remote_status_clean,

        CASE
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) IN ('full-time', 'full time', 'fulltime', 'ft', 'permanent')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%permanent%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%full%'
                THEN 'Full-time'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) IN ('part-time', 'part time', 'parttime', 'pt')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%part%'
                THEN 'Part-time'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) IN ('contract', 'contractor', 'temp', 'temporary', 'freelance', 'c2c')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%contract%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%temp%'
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%freelance%'
                THEN 'Contract'
            WHEN LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) IN ('internship', 'intern', 'co-op', 'coop')
                OR LOWER(TRIM(employment_type)) LIKE '%intern%'
                THEN 'Internship'
            ELSE 'Unknown'
        END AS employment_type_clean


        FROM base
    ),

    -- ── STEP 3: Salary outlier handling ─────────────────────────────
    -- Salary fields contain a few data errors: $0, $1, implausibly high values from mis-parsed hourly-to-annual conversions, or potentially test records. 
    -- Values outside plausible BI/analytics bands are set to NULL (even without salary data, the post itself e.g. skills are useful)
    -- WHERE Annual band:  $20,000 – $500,000
    -- WHERE Hourly band:  $10  – $250
    -- WHERE NOT min > max (data entry error)
    -- WHERE NOT both are set to NULL.
    salaries AS (
        SELECT *,

            CASE
                WHEN CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 20000 AND 500000
                 AND CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 20000 AND 500000
                 AND CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE) <= CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                    THEN CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS annual_salary_min_clean,

            CASE
                WHEN CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 20000 AND 500000
                 AND CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 20000 AND 500000
                 AND CAST(annual_salary_min AS DOUBLE) <= CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                    THEN CAST(annual_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS annual_salary_max_clean,

            CASE
                WHEN CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 10 AND 250
                 AND CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 10 AND 250
                 AND CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE) <= CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                    THEN CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS hourly_salary_min_clean,

            CASE
                WHEN CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 10 AND 250
                 AND CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE) BETWEEN 10 AND 250
                 AND CAST(hourly_salary_min AS DOUBLE) <= CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                    THEN CAST(hourly_salary_max AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS hourly_salary_max_clean

        FROM labeled
    )

    -- ── FINAL SELECT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    -- Replace raw categorical and salary columns with cleaned versions.
    -- All other optional fields (city, soc_code, bls_*, skills, etc.)
    SELECT
        job_id,
        posted_at,
        title,
        normalized_title,
        company_name,
        location_text,
        city,
        city_code,
        state,
        state_code,
        remote_status_clean                          AS remote_status,
        employment_type_clean                        AS employment_type,
        salary_text,
        annual_salary_min_clean                      AS annual_salary_min,
        annual_salary_max_clean                      AS annual_salary_max,
        hourly_salary_min_clean                      AS hourly_salary_min,
        hourly_salary_max_clean                      AS hourly_salary_max,
        soc_code,
        soc_name,
        occupation_family,
        naics_code,
        naics_name,
        onet_code,
        onet_name,
        cip_code,
        cip_name,
        skills,
        program_matches,
        description,
        bls_employment,
        bls_annual_mean_wage,
        bls_annual_median_wage,
        bls_source_year,
        student_signals_work_type,
        student_signals_requirements_summary,
        student_signals_responsibilities_summary,
        student_signals_technical_tools_summary

    FROM salaries

""")

# Register as the canonical SQL view for all downstream analysis
jobs_clean.createOrReplaceTempView("job_facts")
